newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Shell takes over Ogoni hospital in peace move.
newsitem.headline: Shell takes over Ogoni hospital in peace move.

text.p: Royal Dutch Shell Group's Nigerian unit said on Thursday it was taking over maintenance and supply of drugs for the hospital in the troubled Ogoni oil-producing area of Nigeria.
Shell has taken a pounding from international pressure groups since last November when Nigerian authorities hanged nine Ogoni minority rights activists including author Ken Saro-Wiwa.

Shell said in a statement in Lagos that it would provide 28 beds and equipment for Gokana general hospital's operating theatre and laboratories at a cost of 20 million naira. Running costs would amount to 4.5 million naira annually.
"This is the culmination of many months of discussions and meetings with many different communities and opinion leaders in Ogoni land," Shell managing director Brian Anderson said.
"I hope that it marks real progress down the road to reconciliation and is the start of a better relationship based on trust and respect," he added.
Shell, however, maintained that it had no plans as yet to resume oil operations in the area.
"Such a step would be taken only after full discussion and agreement with all Ogoni communities and opinion leaders," Anderson said.
Shell pulled out of the area in 1993 due to hostilities from the host communities.
